paragraphs.source_en: You shall see Him smiling in flowers, then rising and waving His hands in trees.

units.source_en: You shall see Him smiling in flowers, then rising and waving His hands in trees.

paragraphs.source_en: The owl whose night-bound eyes are blind unto the day cannot unveil the mystery of light.

units.source_en: The owl whose night-bound eyes are blind unto the day cannot unveil the mystery of light.

paragraphs.source_en: If you would indeed behold the spirit of death, open your heart wide unto the body of life.

units.source_en: If you would indeed behold the spirit of death, open your heart wide unto the body of life.

paragraphs.source_en: In the depth of your hopes and desires lies your silent knowledge of the beyond;

units.source_en: In the depth of your hopes and desires lies your silent knowledge of the beyond;

paragraphs.source_en: Trust the dreams, for in them is hidden the gate to eternity. Your fear of death is but the trembling of the shepherd when he stands before the king whose hand is to be laid upon him in honour.

units.source_en: Trust the dreams, for in them is hidden the gate to eternity.

paragraphs.source_en: Is the shepherd not joyful beneath his trembling, that he shall wear the mark of the king?

paragraphs.source_en: And what is it to cease breathing, but to free the breath from its restless tides, that it may rise and expand and seek God unencumbered?

paragraphs.source_en: And when the earth shall claim your limbs, then shall you truly dance. And now it was evening.

paragraphs.source_en: And Almitra the seeress said, Blessed be this day and this place and your spirit that has spoken.

paragraphs.source_en: Then he descended the steps of the Temple and all the people followed him. And he reached his ship and stood upon the deck.

paragraphs.source_en: We wanderers, ever seeking the lonelier way, begin no day where we have ended another day; and no sunrise finds us where sunset left us. Even while the earth sleeps we travel.

paragraphs.source_en: We are the seeds of the tenacious plant, and it is in our ripeness and our fullness of heart that we are given to the wind and are scattered.

paragraphs.source_en: But should my voice fade in your ears, and my love vanish in your memory, then I will come again,

paragraphs.source_en: And though death may hide me, and the greater silence enfold me, yet again will I seek your understanding.

paragraphs.source_en: If aught I have said is truth, that truth shall reveal itself in a clearer voice, and in words more kin to your thoughts.
